properties.value: This is a timing side-channel vulnerability in the OCSP policy checking code where a MAC or digest is compared with == instead of a constant-time comparison function, which can leak information through timing differences.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signatures are used throughout the X.509 certificate handling code for digital signatures. While Ed25519 is secure against classical attacks, it is vulnerable to quantum attacks and should be replaced with ML-DSA for post-quantum security.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA signatures are used throughout the X.509 certificate handling code for digital signatures. ECDSA is vulnerable to quantum attacks and should be replaced with ML-DSA for post-quantum security.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 elliptic curve is used in X.509 certificate handling for key exchange and digital signatures. While P-256 is secure against classical attacks, it is vulnerable to quantum attacks and should be replaced with ML-KEM for post-quantum security.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is used in X.509 certificate handling for digest operations. While not directly vulnerable to quantum attacks, SHA-256 is considered legacy and should be upgraded to SHA-3 (SHA3-256) for better long-term security.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-384/512 are used in X.509 certificate handling for digest operations. These are secure hash functions and not directly vulnerable to quantum attacks, but they represent legacy crypto that could be upgraded.

properties.name: pqs:context
